title: 📚 Harvard study: banning phones in schools improves study — but don't expect miracles!
body: 📚 Harvard study: banning phones in schools improves study — but don't expect miracles!
A study led by Harvard University showed that a strict phone ban in schools achieves a real but modest improvement in students' academic achievement.
According to the study, this improvement equals an extra week or two of learning each year — students learn a little more when their phones are not with them in class.
The reason is clear: the phone distracts attention with its notifications and messages, stealing the student's focus without him realising, even if the phone is in his pocket and he doesn't hold it.
But the study warns against exaggerating expectations: banning phones alone will not turn students into top achievers overnight; it is a small step within larger efforts to improve education.
Schools around the world are moving towards tightening phone-use rules, and some collect phones at the school gate and return them at the end of the day.
Simply put: imagine studying with a device in your hand showing you videos and games every minute. Removing it won't make you a genius, but it will give you real extra focus.
Do you support banning phones in schools, or do you see them as a learning tool too?
